title: From Tokens to Cells: Foundation Models for Single-Cell Biology - Akram Baharlouei, Altos Labs
talk_summary: Talk explains single-cell biology data and foundation models, arguing RNA-seq data is noisy and heterogeneous and that expensive transformer models often fail to beat simple baselines. It reports flow-matching models better match distributions and stresses data quality and measurement over raw scale.

takeaways.what_they_do: They benchmarked complex single-cell foundation models against simple linear models and found the expensive models were sometimes no better or worse.
takeaways.evidence_quote: simple linear models are on par or like sometimes even outperforming this

takeaways.technique: Downstream task benchmarks, not model prestige
takeaways.what_they_do: They ran comprehensive NeurIPS benchmarks on multimodal and perturbation tasks and found expensive-to-train models underperformed relative to other domains.
takeaways.evidence_quote: even though these models are very expensive to train... at the end they're not performing as well

takeaways.technique: Data quality and measurement consistency over raw scale
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue single-cell data is noisy and varies across labs/machines, so scaling data without improving quality and measurement realism is insufficient.
takeaways.evidence_quote: important that to work on quality of the data... than just like you know scale the data

takeaways.technique: Evaluate outcome distributions, not just means
takeaways.what_they_do: They contrast flow-matching models that match the data distribution with autoencoder-style models that predict the mean.
takeaways.evidence_quote: trying to predict the mean rather than understanding understanding the distribution
